content: In the field of chemistry, an ethyl group is classified as an alkyl functional group that is derived from ethane (C₂H₆). Its chemical formula is -C₂H₅, and it is frequently abbreviated as -Et. During the mid-20th century in North America, the term ethyl was commonly used to refer to high-performance commercial gasoline that contained lead. This designation originated from the Ethyl Corporation, a company that produced tetraethyl lead, an organometallic compound used as an anti-knock additive in gasoline to improve engine performance. The process of ethylation refers to the chemical formation of a compound through the introduction of the ethyl functional group, C₂H₅, into its molecular structure.
